blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Recent advancements in diffusion models have significantly improved text-to-image generation, enabling their application to visual storytelling, where coherent image sequences are generated from narrative prompts. However, existing methods primarily focus on identity preservation and often fail to adapt to diverse scene variations, resulting in semantic misalignment and structural inflexibility. We propose EOS-Story, a training-free framework that harmonizes identity consistency with scene-specific adaptation across text and vision spaces. In the text space, we decouple the narrative into identity and scene sub-prompts to prevent information dilution, but this leaves the scene without access to appearance cues. To bridge this gap, we introduce Cross-Contextual Bridging, which softly injects a phrase-level appearance residual into the scene's <EOS> embedding. In the vision space, we find that scale mismatch between identity and scene subjects causes a few identity tokens to be repeatedly transferred, producing structural artifacts. We address this with Adaptive Identity Preservation, which anchors identity features at the scene-specific scale (Identity Anchoring) and integrates them via Identity-Aware Self-Attention. To evaluate performance under varied spatial compositions, we extend the Consistory+ benchmark with diverse framing scenarios (Consistory+_+). Extensive experiments show that EOS-Story achieves competitive or superior performance on both benchmarks.
blocks.zh: 最近传播模型的进步大大地改善了文字到图像生成,使得它们能够被应用到视觉故事讲解中,从叙事提示中产生出连贯的图像序列. 然而,现有方法主要注重身份保护,往往无法适应不同的场景变化,导致语义错位和结构上不灵活. 我们提议采用EOS-Story,这是一个无培训框架,将身份一致性与不同文本和视觉空间的场景适应性相协调。 在文本空间中,我们把叙述解为身份和场景子瞬间,以防止信息被稀释,但这让场景无法进入外观提示. 为了弥合这一差距,我们引入了跨文字连接(cross-Contextal Britching),它软地将一个短语级外观残留注入了场景的"EOS"嵌入. 在视觉空间中,我们发现身份和场景主体的尺度不匹配导致一些身份标志被反复地转移,产生出结构文物. 我们用适应性身份保护来解决这个问题,它将身份特征定位在具体地点的尺度(身份识别)上,并通过身份识别-意识自我识别加以整合。 为了评估在各种空间构成下的业绩,我们扩展了Consory+基准,采用不同的框架设想(Consory +_+)。 广泛的实验显示,EOS-Story在两个基准上都取得了有竞争力或优异的表现.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Diffusion models [ 26 , 23 ] have recently advanced the quality of text-to-image generation, enabling diverse applications in visual content creation.
Among these, the visual storytelling task, applicable to digital comics and character-driven animation [ 22 ] , is particularly challenging because it requires aligning with evolving narrative semantics while maintaining a coherent subject across scenes [ 30 ] .
blocks.zh:
传播模型[26,23]最近提升了文本到图像生成的质量,使得视觉内容生成中的应用多样化.
其中,适用于数码漫画和人物驱动动画的视觉故事描述任务[22]尤其具有挑战性,因为它需要与不断演化的叙事语义保持一致,同时在全场保持一个连贯的主题[30].

blocks.en: Figure 1 : Limitations in scene-level adaptation of previous methods. Existing approaches often fail to account for scene-specific variance : (a) semantic misalignment in simple cases, (b) loss of fine-grained prompt details in complex scenarios, and (c) inability to adapt to diverse viewpoints and scales . These issues often lead to repetitive subject structures and weakened alignment with scene-specific prompts. In contrast, our method achieves better scene-level fidelity by adaptively harmonizing identity consistency with the unique context of each scene.

blocks.en:
Recent approaches [ 40 , 17 , 30 ] explicitly design mechanisms to preserve subject identity by transferring subject-relevant features into each scene during generation.
While these methods effectively maintain identity consistency,
they often underrepresent scene-specific variance in both text and vision spaces—the diverse semantic and visual elements that vary across narrative contexts ( Fig. 1 ).
First, at the semantic level, current methods [ 17 , 40 , 30 ] often treat narrative prompts as monolithic inputs, where various semantics (e.g., appearance and scene descriptions) are encoded into a unified embedding.
This can lead to information dilution , making it difficult for the model to uniformly attend to all details [ 14 ] .
As a result, even when a prompt contains rich details (e.g., specific actions or environmental changes), the model often fails to selectively extract scene-specific cues from the prompt.
This directly undermines narrative fidelity, producing scenes that ignore their intended semantics ( Fig. 1 a,b).
Second, at the visual level, existing approaches typically rely on spatially blind feature injection, where identity features are transferred without accounting for the spatial constraints or framing of each scene.
This oversight of structural scene variance (e.g., camera angles or subject scales) can lead to subject inflexibility , such as contextually mismatched poses or repetitive structural patterns across scenes ( Fig. 1 b,c).
Consequently, subjects are rendered with rigid structural patterns that ignore each scene’s intended layout, further weakening alignment with scene-specific prompts.
Therefore, achieving coherent storytelling requires scene-specific adaptation, where identity consistency is harmonized with the semantic and structural variance of each scene.

最近的方法[40,17,30]明确设计机制,通过在生成过程中将主题相关特征转移到每个场景来保存主题特征.
虽然这些方法有效地保持了身份一致性,

首先,在语义层面,当前的方法[17,40,30]经常将叙事提示作为单文输入,其中各种语义(如外观和场景描述)被编码为统一的嵌入.
这可能导致信息稀释,使模型难以统一处理所有细节[14].
因此,即使一个提示包含丰富的细节(例如具体行动或环境变化),该模型也往往无法有选择地从提示中提取特定场景的提示.
这直接破坏了叙事忠贞,产生了无视其意图的语义的场景(图1a,b).
第二,在视觉层面,现有方法通常依赖于空间盲特征注入,即身份特征的转移,而不考虑每个场景的空间限制或框架。
这种对结构场景差异(如相机角度或主题尺度)的监督可能导致主题不灵活,例如背景不匹配的场景或跨场景的重复结构模式(图1b,c).
因此,主题的结构模式僵化,忽略了每个场景的预定布局,进一步削弱了与场景特定提示的配合。
因此,实现连贯的故事叙述需要场景特定的改编,其中身份一致性与每个场景的语义和结构差异一致.

blocks.en:
To address this issue, we propose EOS-Story , a framework designed to adaptively account for scene-specific variance via two complementary modules, (1) Cross-Contextual Bridging: We hypothesize that semantic misalignment arises when long and complex prompts are encoded holistically, causing scene-varying attributes to be diluted [ 16 , 14 ] .
Rather than encoding all information in a single prompt, we decouple the narrative into an identity prompt describing the subject and a scene prompt describing the scenario.
For instance, “a woman with blond hair reading a book.” is split into an identity prompt (“a woman with blond hair.”) and a scene prompt (“a woman reading a book.”).
However, this separation introduces a new challenge: since the scene prompt contains no appearance information, the subject generated within the scene has no way to reflect the actual target identity.
To bridge this semantic gap without reverting to monolithic encoding, we preserve the scene sub-prompt as a semantic anchor and softly inject appearance information at the embedding level.
Motivated by the strong generative influence and summarization ability of ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embeddings [ 20 , 37 ] ,
we interpret it not merely as a terminal token, but as a residual-based semantic control point for scene-aware storytelling ( Sec. 3.1 ).
Unlike prior EOS-based methods that substitute the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding between prompts differing by a single word (e.g., an object class) [ 9 , 20 ] , we capture a phrase-level appearance difference
and infuse it into the scene’s ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle , reflecting rich multi-attribute cues without explicit word-level repetition ( Sec. 3.2 ).
This provides the scene image with the specified appearance cues at the semantic level, enabling more effective feature-level identity transfer.

blocks.en:
(2) Adaptive Identity Preservation: To mitigate subject inflexibility induced by spatially blind feature transfer, we introduce a spatially adaptive identity injection mechanism that better aligns identity features with the scene-specific layout ( Sec. 3.3 ).
We observe that the scale mismatch between identity and scene subjects prevents various identity tokens from corresponding to the scene tokens.
As a result, only a few identity tokens are repeatedly transferred to the scene and cause structural artifacts.
Motivated by this, we apply Identity Anchoring, which adaptively resizes identity features to match the intended framing and scale of the scene.
This enforces structural compatibility between identity and scene representations, reducing scale-induced distortions ( Fig. 10 b).
We then refine the integration through Identity-Aware Self-Attention, which enables scene features to selectively attend to subject features, building upon [ 30 ] .
Unlike existing spatially blind transfer strategies [ 30 , 17 , 40 ] , our approach supports scene-conditioned variation in subject structure (e.g., viewpoint changes) while preserving core identity characteristics.
To evaluate scene-specific structural variance, we introduce Consistory+_+, extending Consistory+ [ 17 ] with diverse framing prompts [ 15 ] to simulate the realistic framing shifts of real-world storytelling.
We validate our method on Consistory+ and Consistory+_+, demonstrating consistently improved performance under framing variations.
Our contributions are as follows: • We show that the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding can carry phrase-level,
multi-attribute information, enabling appearance cues to be infused during generation. • We propose EOS-Story , a training-free framework with two modules: Cross-Contextual Bridging (text-space semantic recomposition)
and Adaptive Identity Preservation (vision-space scale-aware transfer). • We introduce Consistory+_+ , an extended benchmark with diverse
framing phrases, and demonstrate consistent improvements over existing
approaches on both the original and extended benchmarks.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Visual Storytelling. With the advancement of diffusion models [ 26 , 23 ] , their applications have expanded into various domains.
To meet users’ needs for generating images that preserve subject identity, numerous personalization methods have been proposed [ 1 , 36 , 13 , 7 , 28 , 11 ] .
However, these approaches primarily focus on preserving subject appearance [ 30 ] , often overlooking how the subject should adapt across different visual contexts.
To bridge this gap, visual storytelling [ 40 , 17 , 25 , 19 , 33 ] has emerged as a compelling paradigm for generating identity-consistent images across diverse and dynamic scenes [ 17 ] .
Some methods fine-tune diffusion models to explicitly capture subject identity [ 33 , 25 ] , while [ 40 , 30 , 17 , 19 , 34 , 8 ] explore training-free strategies that leverage intermediate features from the attention mechanism.
For example, Consistory [ 30 ] directly maps subject identity across different scenes to achieve identity consistency, while 1P1S [ 17 ] leverages the context consistency of CLIP [ 24 ] and transfers this information through the cross-attention mechanism.
However, these methods prioritize identity consistency at the cost of scene adaptation, often producing rigid subject depictions and weak prompt alignment.
While concurrent works [ 8 , 34 ] attempt to alleviate subject rigidity, they still delegate prompt alignment to the underlying diffusion model.
In contrast, we find that faithful scene adaptation depends not only on the vision space but also on the text space, and design our framework to jointly address both—improving prompt alignment through semantic-level residual injection and adapting to structural variance through scale-aware feature transfer.
blocks.zh:
视觉故事解说. 随着传播模式[26,23]的推进,其应用已扩展到多个领域.
为了满足用户生成保存主题身份的图像的需要,提出了许多个性化方法[1、36、13、7、28、11]。
然而,这些方法主要侧重于保留主题外观[30],往往忽略主题应如何适应不同的视觉环境。
为了弥合这一差距,视觉故事讲法[40、17、25、19、33]已成为在各种动态场景中产生符合身份的图像的令人信服的范例[17]。
一些方法微调传播模式,以明确捕捉主体特征[33,25],而[40,30,17,19,34,8]则探索利用关注机制的中间特征的无培训策略.
例如,Consistory [30] 直接绘制不同场景的主体身份图,以实现身份一致性,而1P1S [17] 则利用CLIP[24]的上下文一致性,并通过交叉注意机制传输这些信息.
然而,这些方法以场景改编为代价,优先确定身份一致性,往往产生僵硬的主题描述和微弱的快速对齐.
虽然同时进行的工作[8,34]试图缓解主题僵硬性,但它们仍然使迅速与基本传播模式保持一致。
相反,我们发现,忠实的场景适应不仅取决于视觉空间,还取决于文字空间,并设计了我们的框架,以便联合处理两种问题——通过语义层面的剩余注入来改进迅速的对齐,并通过具有规模意识的特征转移来适应结构差异。

blocks.en:
⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle Embedding in Diffusion Models. In CLIP [ 24 ] , which is widely used to encode text in text-to-image generation models, the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle token encapsulates a contextual summary of the entire prompt [ 37 ] . Recent mechanistic analyses [ 31 ] further show that padding tokens, including ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle , carry non-trivial semantic influence in text-to-image generation.
Built upon this, [ 37 ] demonstrates that ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle has dominant influence in image generation: replacing the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding of an original prompt (e.g., “A blue bird”) with that of a target prompt (e.g., “A blue chair”) can steer the generated image toward the target semantics.
Motivated by this property, several works [ 9 , 20 , 12 ] have utilized ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle or text-embedding manipulation for downstream tasks.
Specifically, [ 9 ] substitutes ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle to resolve semantic binding issues in object–attribute prompts, [ 20 ] injects the entire base prompt embedding along with ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle into the position of specific objects to perform image editing, and [ 12 ] manipulates text embeddings to suppress unwanted content.
Unlike prior methods that either substitute ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle between prompts differing by a single word [ 9 , 20 ] or manipulate embeddings for content removal [ 12 ] , we use ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle as a scene-aware interface to transfer phrase-level appearance information into scene-specific prompt representations for visual storytelling.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en:
Overview. To achieve identity consistency while allowing subjects to adapt to diverse scenes, we propose EOS-Story ( Fig. 3 ), a framework that models scene-specific variance in two complementary spaces.
(1) Cross-Contextual Bridging (CCB) addresses semantic variance by transferring phrase-level appearance cues into the scene context through the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding, mitigating information dilution in long and complex prompts.
(2) Adaptive Identity Preservation (AIP) addresses structural variance by aligning identity features to each scene’s subject scale (Identity Anchoring), followed by Identity-Aware Self-Attention refinement.
blocks.zh:
概览. 为了实现身份一致性,同时让主体适应不同的场景,我们提出EOS-Story(图3),这个框架在两个互补空间中模拟场景特异性差异.
(1) 跨文字 Bridgeing(CCB)通过\\langle EOS\\rangle嵌入,将短语级的外观提示移到场景上下文,解决语义差异,在长而复杂的提示中减轻信息稀释.
(2) 适应性身份保全(AIP)通过将身份特征与每个场景的主题尺度(身份识别安魂曲)相配合来解决结构差异,然后是身份识别-Aware自我识别的完善.

blocks.zh: 3.1 评价处 嵌入为语义处理

blocks.en:
We first test whether the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding can serve as a global semantic control point.
As shown in Fig. 2 a, adding an attribute embedding (e.g., “black”) at different token positions of a base prompt (“A photo of a dog”) produces notably different outcomes.
Directly adding the attribute embedding to the target word token (“dog”) fails to alter the output, and even a broad injection across all non-EOS tokens produces only minor changes.
In contrast, injecting the attribute only into the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding induces a clear semantic shift, suggesting that the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding serves as an effective handle for embedding-level semantic editing during generation.

blocks.en:
We further examine whether semantic changes can be composed at the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle level through additive and subtractive operations ( Fig. 2 b).
Simple subtraction often yields incomplete edits, likely because unchanged word-level tokens continue to preserve the original semantics ( Fig. 2 b2), whereas addition and replacement more reliably induce coherent semantic shifts.
Notably, our observation is that the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding can capture not only a single attribute [ 9 , 20 ] but also multiple semantic factors , simultaneously affecting actions and environments through one EOS-level edit ( Fig. 2 b3).
These edits occur without modifying the word-level tokens, indicating that semantic adjustments at the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle level can override or complement persistent token-level semantics.
These observations suggest that the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding provides a context-preserving handle that can encode rich, multi-attribute semantics through a residual operation.
Motivated by this, we design Cross-Contextual Bridging, which transfers phrase-level appearance information into each scene’s ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding, allowing subject-specific appearance cues to be integrated while maintaining the scene context.

blocks.en: 3.2 Cross-Contextual Bridging
blocks.zh: 3.2 跨文字 桥梁

blocks.en:
To avoid treating a story prompt as a single monolithic description, we construct reference subprompts from structured storyboard inputs (e.g., Consistory+ benchmark [ 17 ] ).
Each input is decomposed into four semantic components: style , subject , appearance , and scene .
Encoding all components as a single prompt (e.g., “ A majestic winter-themed artwork of a regal snow queen in icy beauty watching over a frozen kingdom. ”) can dilute fine-grained appearance cues in long and compositionally complex descriptions [ 14 ] .
To recover such appearance cues without lengthening the scene prompt, we construct three reference subprompts around a minimal shared context:
(1) Style Prompt : Style + Subject,
(2) Identity Prompt : Style + Subject + Appearance , and
(3) Scene Prompt : Style + Subject + Scene .
The shared Style + Subject prompt serves as the minimal anchor for measuring appearance-specific displacement before transferring it to each scene prompt.
This anchor is scene-independent, while still preserving the subject slot and visual style, making it suitable for defining an appearance cue that can be shared across all scenes.

为避免将一个故事提示作为单一单词描述,我们从结构化的故事板输入(如Consistory+基准[17])中构建了参考子瞬态.
每个输入被分解为四个语义部分:样式,主题,外观,和场景.
将所有部件编码为单一的提示(例如“冰冷美景中的蓝藻雪女王的严酷冬季主题艺术品”)可以淡化长篇和结构复杂的描述中的精细外观提示[14]。
为了恢复这种外观提示,而不迅速延长场景,我们围绕一个最小的共享上下文构建了三个参考子提示:
(1)样式提示:样式+主题,
(2) 身份提示:样式+主题+外观,以及
(3)场景提示:样式+主题+场景.
共享样式 + 主题 提示作为测量外观特定位置的最小锚点,然后立即将其转移到每个场景。
这个主播是场景独立的,同时仍然保留主题槽和视觉风格,使其适合定义一个可以在所有场景中共享的外观提示.

blocks.en:
By keeping the scene prompt free of explicit appearance phrases, we preserve the scene description as the primary semantic context.
Cross-Contextual Bridging then reintroduces the missing appearance cue at the embedding level.
This allows the subject appearance to be recovered without modifying the word-level scene description.
Building on our empirical observations ( Sec. 3.1 and Appendix 0.A ), we utilize the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding as a controllable semantic handle, enabling phrase-level appearance transfer without increasing the textual length of the scene description.
We obtain the corresponding ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embeddings, e ​ o ​ s s ​ t ​ y eos_{sty} , e ​ o ​ s i ​ d eos_{id} , and e ​ o ​ s s ​ c eos_{sc} , from the CLIP [ 24 ] text encoder.
Although e ​ o ​ s i ​ d eos_{id} contains the desired appearance information, directly adding it to e ​ o ​ s s ​ c eos_{sc} can redundantly reinforce the shared style and subject semantics, leading to unintended semantic drift.
We therefore define the appearance residual as the local displacement from the shared style-subject anchor to the identity prompt, following the approximate linearity of CLIP embedding space [ 32 ] : Δ a ​ p ​ p = e ​ o ​ s i ​ d − e ​ o ​ s s ​ t ​ y \Delta_{app}=eos_{id}-eos_{sty} .
We transport this residual to the scene prompt by constructing the infused embedding e ​ o ​ s i ​ n ​ f eos_{inf} : e ​ o ​ s i ​ n ​ f = e ​ o ​ s s ​ c + Δ a ​ p ​ p . eos_{inf}=eos_{sc}+\Delta_{app}. (1) We replace each scene ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding e ​ o ​ s s ​ c eos_{sc} with its infused counterpart e ​ o ​ s i ​ n ​ f eos_{inf} .
The identity prompt embedding and the modified scene prompt embedding are then fed into the diffusion model for the subsequent feature-level identity transfer.
This formulation restores subject appearance cues within the scene prompt representation while preserving the original scene semantics.
This appearance-aware representation further reduces the semantic gap between the scene subject and its identity counterpart before feature injection, providing a stronger basis for the subsequent feature-level identity transfer ( Sec. 3.3 ).

blocks.en:

To achieve natural subject alignment across scenes, we transfer visual features from the identity image x i ​ d ∈ ℝ H ​ W × C x_{id}\in\mathbb{R}^{HW\times C} to N N scene images { x s ​ c n } n = 1 N ∈ ℝ N × H ​ W × C \{x_{sc}^{n}\}_{n=1}^{N}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times HW\times C} .
We use intermediate features from the first decoder block of the U-Net, where coarse spatial structure is known to emerge [ 29 ] , to establish correspondence between identity and scene subject regions.
Identity Anchoring is applied during early denoising stages, when global layout is primarily established, so that later steps can refine fine-grained details without disrupting the aligned structure.
During generation, we obtain subject masks ℳ i ​ d ∈ ℝ H ​ W × 1 \mathcal{M}_{id}\in\mathbb{R}^{HW\times 1} and { ℳ s ​ c n } n = 1 N ∈ ℝ N × H ​ W × 1 \{\mathcal{M}_{sc}^{n}\}_{n=1}^{N}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times HW\times 1} from the cross-attention maps of the corresponding subject tokens.

blocks.en:
Building upon the empirical observation in Sec. 3.1 that the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding acts as a global semantic control point, we conduct a quantitative evaluation in addition to providing qualitative samples.
As shown in Tab. 2 , injecting appearance information solely into the subject token fails to reliably encode identity cues.
Distributing the same information across all non-EOS tokens partially improves alignment, yet the gains remain limited, suggesting that localized token-level injection struggles to propagate appearance semantics consistently during generation.
In contrast, modifying only the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding consistently achieves the highest text–image alignment and perceptual similarity.
These results indicate that semantic control is more effectively exercised at the EOS level, where global context is integrated, rather than at individual word tokens that contribute only localized representations.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
In this work, we propose EOS-Story , a training-free framework that adaptively models scene-specific variance in visual storytelling across text and vision spaces. We introduce Cross-Contextual Bridging , which decouples the narrative into identity and scene sub-prompts and bridges the resulting semantic gap by injecting phrase-level appearance residuals into the scene’s ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding. To complement this with structural adaptation, we further propose Adaptive Identity Preservation , which anchors subject features at the scene-specific scale and refines integration through Identity-Aware Self-Attention. To evaluate scene adaptability, we extend Consistory+ with diverse framing variations (Consistory+_+).
Extensive experiments show that EOS-Story achieves competitive or superior performance in both prompt fidelity and structural adaptability.

Empirical Analysis of EOS Linearity. Although prior work has shown that CLIP text embeddings often exhibit approximate linear compositionality over semantic factors [ 32 ] , it is non-trivial whether the same property holds at the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle hidden state, which aggregates contextual information through causal attention rather than being a simple sum of word embeddings. Rather than assuming exact linearity, we empirically examine whether the appearance residual Δ a ​ p ​ p = e ​ o ​ s i ​ d − e ​ o ​ s s ​ t ​ y \Delta_{app}=eos_{id}-eos_{sty} behaves as a transferable semantic direction.
To this end, we construct a large prompt set spanning diverse subjects, styles, and scenes, with appearance attributes of varying complexity—from short phrases to long relational descriptions ( Fig. 11 ).

为此,我们构建了一个涵盖不同主题、风格和场景的大型快速集,其外观特征复杂程度各异——从短短语到长关系描述(图11)。

Residuals extracted from the same attribute but different subjects remain highly aligned, whereas residuals from different attributes are clearly separated.
This indicates that Δ a ​ p ​ p \Delta_{app} captures a subject-agnostic appearance direction rather than subject-specific content.

Transferability. We then add a Δ a ​ p ​ p \Delta_{app} extracted from one subject to the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle of a different prompt which only contains subject and scene descriptions, and compare it against the embedding of an explicit prompt (subject + appearance + scene) that states the attribute in words ( transfer target ).
The two are highly similar, while both the appearance-free base and a mismatched random attribute are clearly distinguished.
Notably, this holds even for long, compositional phrases, indicating that EOS-level residuals transfer rich appearance semantics—not merely single words—in a linear manner.

Generative effect. Finally, scaling the injected residual as e ​ o ​ s s ​ c + λ ⋅ Δ a ​ p ​ p eos_{sc}+\lambda\cdot\Delta_{app} progressively strengthens the target appearance in the generated image ( Fig. 11 , bottom): as λ \lambda increases, the attribute (e.g., round glasses) emerges and intensifies, confirming that the residual exerts a controllable, monotonic influence on generation.
Together, these results show that Δ a ​ p ​ p \Delta_{app} functions as a subject-agnostic, transferable, and controllable appearance direction—justifying our EOS-level residual manipulation.

To investigate this, we compute the pairwise cosine similarity between e ​ o ​ s o ​ r ​ g eos_{org} and e ​ o ​ s i ​ n ​ f eos_{inf} across samples ( Fig. 14 ), under the hypothesis that significant semantic shifts would result in low similarity.

We further support this with a t-SNE visualization ( Fig. 15 ), where e ​ o ​ s i ​ n ​ f eos_{inf} embeddings consistently cluster near their e ​ o ​ s o ​ r ​ g eos_{org} counterparts.
Together with qualitative examples ( Fig. 13 ) showing improved attention localization, these results suggest that the infused ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle embedding effectively combines essential semantics while remaining close to the original semantic configuration.

As shown in bottom of Fig. 14 , the similarity remains consistently high ( μ = 0.9407 \mu=0.9407 ), indicating that the Cross-Contextual Bridging mechanism can be used across different text encoder configurations.

blocks.en:
Additional Variants of the EOS-Based Control. We further analyze variations of EOS-based semantic control in Tab. 6 .
Beyond the main variant presented in the primary experiments ( Tab. 3 ), we systematically examine different EOS construction strategies by varying the base EOS components, injected directions, and mixing weights.
Specifically, Δ a ​ p ​ p \Delta_{app} ( Tab. 6 C) corresponds to directly replacing the EOS embedding with the appearance residual, following [ 9 ] .
The configuration e ​ o ​ s s ​ c o ​ r ​ g + e ​ o ​ s a ​ p ​ p o ​ r ​ g + e ​ o ​ s s ​ t ​ y o ​ r ​ g eos_{sc}^{org}+eos_{app}^{org}+eos_{sty}^{org} naively concatenates EOS embeddings obtained from each phrase-level component in the benchmark.
The relatively lower performance of Δ a ​ p ​ p \Delta_{app} can be attributed to the absence of scene information in the resulting embedding.
While another variant e ​ o ​ s i ​ d + Δ s ​ c eos_{id}+\Delta_{sc} is mathematically similar to our additive formulation, it exhibits slightly reduced alignment.
We hypothesize that this variant introduces multiple semantic directions originating from overlapping bases,
whereas our formulation injects a consistent appearance residual Δ a ​ p ​ p \Delta_{app} into multiple scene-grounded ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle anchors { e ​ o ​ s s ​ c n } n = 1 N \{eos_{sc}^{n}\}_{n=1}^{N} .
By shifting several scene embeddings along a consistent semantic direction, our approach maintains a structured integration of narrative context and appearance cues.
This parallel infusion results in more stable semantic control and ultimately improves text–image alignment compared to subject-anchored alternatives.
Overall, these results indicate that simply replacing or naively combining EOS components does not sufficiently preserve semantic grounding. In contrast, controlled injection of the appearance direction into a scene-aware EOS consistently improves text alignment, highlighting the importance of structured and context-preserving semantic modulation.

blocks.en:
The ShotBench [ 15 ] includes a wide range of framing phrases across eight categories ( Tab. 7 ).
To ensure a focused and rigorous evaluation of scene-specific structural variance, we intentionally restricted the scope to three primary categories, excluding the remaining five based on the following methodological criteria: (1) Prompt Redundancy: Shot Framing descriptors (e.g., “single”, “2 shot”) primarily specify the number of characters, which is already inherently defined by the subject phrases in the storyboard prompts; (2) Redundancy Mitigation: Lens Size phrases (e.g., “wide lens”) are largely redundant as they are semantically encompassed by the Shot Size category (“wide shot”); (3) Domain Incompatibility: Camera Movement is inherently applicable to temporal video sequences and is thus irrelevant to static image generation; and (4) Task Relevance: Lighting-related categories fall outside the scope of our work, as they primarily focus on stylistic or artistic variations rather than the structural and compositional elements that define scene-specific variance.
blocks.zh:

为确保对具体地点的结构差异进行集中和严格的评价,我们有意将范围限制在三个主要类别,不包括根据以下方法标准确定的其余五个类别: (1) 即时冗余:Shot Flaming描述符(如“单镜头”,“2镜头”)主要指定字符数,而故事板提示符中的主题短语已对字符数作了内在的定义;(2) 冗余缓解:Lens Space 短语(如“广镜头”)基本上是冗余的,因为它们被Shot Spise 分类(“广镜头”)所囊括; (3)域不兼容性:相机运动本质上适用于时空视频序列,因此与静态图像生成无关;(4)任务关联性:与照明相关的类别不属于我们的工作范畴,因为它们主要侧重于风格或艺术的变异,而不是定义场景特异性的结构和组成要素.

blocks.en:
Framing Phrase Filtering. Although SDXL generally produces textually well-aligned images, it sometimes struggles to accurately reflect specific framing phrases.
Before incorporating these phrases into our benchmark extension, we first evaluate how well they are captured by the base SDXL model using the ShotBench evaluation mechanism.
To quantitatively assess phrase reflection, we construct approximately 90 diverse scene prompts and append each framing phrase at the end (e.g., “A photo of a woman baking cookies, close-up shot”).
We generate images for 10 random seeds per phrase and compute the top-1 and top-3 accuracy, along with standard deviations, as shown in Fig. 16 .
For example, in the “shot size” category with 7 phrase options, this results in a total of 6,300 images (90 scenes × 7 phrases × 10 seeds).
We filter out framing phrases whose top-1 accuracy is zero (e.g., “extreme wide shot”), as these are not reliably reflected in the generated outputs from SDXL.

在将这些短语纳入我们的基准扩展之前,我们首先利用Shot Bench评估机制,评价这些短语如何被基础SDXL模型捕获。
为了定量评估短语的反射,我们构建了大约90个不同的场景提示,并在结尾附加每个框架短语(例如“妇女烘焙饼干的照片,特写镜头”)。
我们为每个短语生成10个随机种子的图像,并计算最高-1和最高-3的精度,以及标准偏差,如图16所示。
例如,在带有7个短语选项的"镜头大小"类别中,这导致总共6300幅图像(90场景×7个短语×10个种子).

Then, the model is instructed to append the most appropriate framing phrase for the given scene, resulting in Consistory+_+.

Framing Accuracy Evaluation. Following the evaluation protocol in [ 15 ] , we provide the generated image along with the corresponding framing category (e.g., shot size) and prompt the model with a multiple-choice question.
For instance, for shot size evaluation, we prompt the model with a multiple-choice question such as
“What is the shot size of this shot?” and provide predefined options (e.g., wide shot, medium shot, close-up shot).
The predicted category is compared against the framing phrase specified in the text prompt, and accuracy is reported.

SD3 Applicability. We use the Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large weights with a CFG scale of 4.5 and 28 sampling steps.
In SDXL, identity information is incorporated via extended attention, where the subject key and value embeddings are concatenated with those of the scene. However, in DiT-based models, fixed positional encodings and sequence-length constraints make such direct concatenation non-trivial [ 3 , 18 ] .
To address this architectural difference, we compute attention along two parallel paths: (i) the original scene query–key–value path and (ii) a subject-referenced path using the scene query with subject key and value embeddings. The resulting attention outputs are then combined, enabling implicit identity referencing without modifying the positional encoding structure.
Despite the architectural adaptation, the core semantic control mechanism remains intact. As shown in Fig. 25 and Sec. 0.C.2 , our method consistently improves alignment, demonstrating its applicability to DiT-based diffusion models.
blocks.zh:
SD3应用. 我们使用稳定扩散3.5的大型重量,CFG尺度为4.5和28个取样步骤。
在SDXL中,身份信息通过扩大关注来整合,其中主题密钥和价值嵌入与场景的密钥和价值结合. 然而,在基于DiT的模型中,固定位置编码和序列长的制约使得这种直接的交配[3,18].
为了解决这种建筑差异,我们按照两个平行路径计算注意力:(一) 原始的场景查询 - 键 - 值路径和(二) 利用场景查询使用主题键和值嵌入的标的参考路径. 由此产生的注意产出随后被合并,从而能够隐含身份参考而不修改位置编码结构。
尽管进行了建筑改造,核心语义控制机制仍然完好无损. 如图25和Sec.0.C.2所示,我们的方法不断改进对齐性,表明它适用于基于DiT的传播模型。

We therefore apply only the AIP module to FLUX, which is model-agnostic by design.

Recent large pretrained image editing model FLUX-Kontext exhibits strong identity-preservation capabilities and can be directly applied to visual storytelling.
However, we observe that it remains anchored to the reference, producing copy-and-paste-style synthesis that fails to follow scene-specific prompts ( Fig. 26 , Tab. 12 ).
As shown in Tab. 12 , while it achieves strong identity scores (e.g., CLIP-I, DreamSim), its prompt alignment (CLIP-T) and overall quality remain limited, indicating that identity preservation alone is insufficient for storytelling—scene-specific adaptation is essential.
We further compare with CharaConsist [ 34 ] , a recent FLUX-based storytelling method. Since its evaluation benchmark is not publicly available, we compare on Consistory+ for a fair setting. EOS-Story achieves competitive or superior performance across both identity and prompt-alignment metrics, demonstrating that our scene-adaptive design transfers effectively to FLUX.

最近的大型预训图像编辑模型FLUX-Kontext显示出强大的身份保护能力,可以直接应用于视觉故事讲述.

blocks.en: Appendix 0.D Limitation & Future Work
blocks.zh: 附录0.D 限制和今后的工作

blocks.en:
Although our model effectively balances prompt and subject coherence, several limitations remain.
While the cross-attention map generally captures subject regions accurately, it occasionally fails to attend to the correct area, leading to misaligned or partially misplaced generations—issues also observed in previous works.
This can be handled by explicitly using the subject mask as an additional condition.
In addition, there are cases where the model fails to generate accurate images at all (e.g., Fig. 30 “faun”), which appears to be an inherent limitation of the underlying SDXL backbone.
Furthermore, since Cross-Contextual Bridging exploits the contextual summarization property of the CLIP ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle token, it does not directly transfer to models based on T5 or LLM-based text encoders, where the ⟨ \langle EOS ⟩ \rangle token no longer serves a comparable role. Enabling analogous residual-based semantic composition on such encoders is a promising direction for extending our framework to a broader range of modern diffusion models.

可以通过明确使用主体口罩作为附加条件来处理.
此外,在有些情况下,模型根本无法产生准确的图像(例如图30“faun”),这似乎是SDXL主干线的固有限制。
此外,由于跨文本 连接利用 CLIP \ langle EOS \\rangle 符号的上下文总和属性,它不会直接转移到基于T5或基于 LLM 的文本编码器的模型上,其中\\ langle EOS \\rangle 符号不再起到可比的作用. 使这种编码器具有类似的剩余语义组成,是将我们的框架扩大到更广泛的现代传播模式的一个有希望的方向。
